The first line of walls is a wide enclosure corresponding to the first Muslim military camp, used as shelter for the population in case of siege. For this task it was provided with large [cisterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cistern "Cistern").

The first enclosure is separated by the second one by the so-called _Muro de la Vela_ ("Wall of the Sail"), taking its name from a bell that warned the population in case of events such as the arrival of a ship in the port, danger, fires etc. This wall was built by King [Charles III of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III_of_Spain "Charles III of Spain").

In the second enclosure was the residence for the governors, their soldiers and their servants. It included also the mosque, baths, tanks, tents etc.

The third enclosure, the most external, is also the most modern in the complex. After the Christian reconquest of Almería, the [Catholic monarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_monarchs "Catholic monarchs")[Isabella I of Castile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabella_I_of_Castile "Isabella I of Castile") and [Ferdinand II of Aragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_II_of_Aragon "Ferdinand II of Aragon") had a castle built in the most elevated sector of the town, more apt to resist the new gunpowder [artillery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artillery "Artillery").

## Cinema

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Cinema")]

The Alcazaba has been used to film _[Conan the Barbarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan\_the\_Barbarian\_(1982\_film) "Conan the Barbarian (1982 film)")_,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-3)_[Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana\_Jones\_and\_the\_Last\_Crusade "Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade")_,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-4)_[Never Say Never Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never\_Say\_Never\_Again "Never Say Never Again")_,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-5) and most recently _[Wonder Woman 1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder\_Woman\_1984 "Wonder Woman 1984")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-8) The syndicated TV series _[Queen of Swords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen\_of\_Swords\_(TV\_series) "Queen of Swords (TV series)")_ used the inner courtyard and gardens.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-9)

The [sixth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_of_Thrones_(season_6) "Game of Thrones (season 6)") of the TV series _[Game of Thrones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game\_of\_Thrones "Game of Thrones")_ was shot in locations from Andalusia to Catalonia, including the Muralla de Jayrán,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-10) and the Alcazaba fortress, which is the capital of [Dorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorne "Dorne"), the kingdom of the [House Martell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Martell "House Martell").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcazaba_of_Almer%C3%ADa#cite_note-11)

**Slug** or **land slug** is a [common name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_name "Common name") for any apparently [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell "Gastropod shell")-less [terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_mollusc "Terrestrial mollusc")[gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod "Gastropod")[mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc "Mollusc"). The word _slug_ is also often used as part of the common name of any gastropod mollusc that has no shell, a very reduced shell, or only a small internal shell, particularly [sea slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slug "Sea slug") and [semi-slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-slug "Semi-slug") (this is in contrast to the common name _[snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail "Snail")_, which applies to gastropods that have a coiled shell large enough that they can fully retract their soft parts into it).

Various [taxonomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology) "Taxonomy (biology)")[families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(taxonomy) "Family (taxonomy)") of land slugs form part of several quite different evolutionary lineages, which also include snails. Thus, the various families of slugs are not closely related, despite the superficial similarity in overall body form. The shell-less condition has arisen many times independently as an example of [convergent evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convergent_evolution "Convergent evolution"), and thus the category "slug" is [polyphyletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyphyly "Polyphyly").

## Taxonomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Taxonomy")]

Of the six orders of [Pulmonata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonata "Pulmonata"), two – the [Onchidiacea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onchidiacea "Onchidiacea") and [Soleolifera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soleolifera "Soleolifera") – solely comprise slugs. A third group, the [Sigmurethra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmurethra "Sigmurethra"), contains various clades of snails, semi-slugs (i.e. snails whose shells are too small for them to retract fully into), and slugs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Burton1982-1) The taxonomy of this group is in the process of being revised in light of DNA sequencing.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-White2011-2) Research suggests that pulmonates are paraphyletic and basal to the [opisthobranchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch "Opisthobranch"), which are a terminal branch of the tree.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-3) The family [Ellobiidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellobiidae "Ellobiidae") are also polyphyletic.

## Description

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Description")]

[![Image 7: Drawing of slug with labels for the foot (bottom side), the foot fringe that surrounds it, the mantle behind the head, the pneumostome for breathing, and the optical and sensory tentacles](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Slug_parts.png/330px-Slug_parts.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Slug_parts.png)

The external anatomy of a slug

The external anatomy of a slug includes the following:

*   **Tentacles**: Like other pulmonate land gastropods, the majority of land slugs have two pairs of 'feelers' or _tentacles_ on their head. The upper pair is light-sensing and has eyespots at the ends, while the lower pair provides the [sense of smell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olfaction "Olfaction"). Both pairs are retractable in [stylommatophoran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stylommatophora "Stylommatophora") slugs, but contractile in [veronicellid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronicellidae "Veronicellidae") slugs.
*   **Mantle**: On top of the slug, behind the head, is the saddle-shaped _[mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mantle\_(mollusc) "Mantle (mollusc)")_. In stylommatophoran slugs, on the right-hand side of the mantle is a [respiratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory "Respiratory") opening, the [pneumostome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumostome "Pneumostome"), which is easier to see when open; also on the right side at the front are the genital opening and anus. [Veronicellid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronicellidae "Veronicellidae") slugs have a mantle covering the whole dorsal part of the body, they have no respiratory opening, and the anus opens posteriorly.
*   **Tail**: The part of a slug behind the mantle is called the 'tail'.
*   **Keel**: Some species of slugs, for example _[Tandonia budapestensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandonia\_budapestensis "Tandonia budapestensis")_, have a prominent ridge running over their back along the middle of the tail (sometimes along the whole tail, sometimes only the posterior part).
*   **Foot**: The bottom side of a slug, which is flat, is called the 'foot'. Like almost all gastropods, a slug moves by rhythmic waves of [muscular contraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscular_contraction "Muscular contraction") on the underside of its foot. It simultaneously secretes a layer of [mucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucus "Mucus") that it travels on, which helps prevent damage to the foot tissues.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-biologists1-4) Around the edge of the foot in some slugs is a structure called the 'foot fringe'.
*   **Vestigial shell**: Most slugs retain a remnant of their shell, which is usually internalized. This organ generally serves as storage for calcium salts, often in conjunction with the digestive glands.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Loest1979-5) An internal shell is present in the [Limacidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limacidae "Limacidae")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Branson1980-6) and Parmacellidae.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-7) Adult [Philomycidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomycidae "Philomycidae"),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Branson1980-6)[Onchidiidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onchidiidae "Onchidiidae")[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-8) and [Veronicellidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veronicellidae "Veronicellidae")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-9) lack shells.

## Physiology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Physiology")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Ambigolimax.jpg/250px-Ambigolimax.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ambigolimax.jpg)

An active _[Ambigolimax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambigolimax "Ambigolimax")_ slug in [Fremont, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fremont,_California "Fremont, California")

Slugs' bodies are made up mostly of water and, without a full-sized shell, their soft tissues are prone to [desiccation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desiccation "Desiccation"). They must generate protective mucus to survive. Many species are most active following rainfall or during nighttime since there is increased moisture on the ground. In drier conditions, they hide in damp places such as under [tree bark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_bark "Tree bark"), fallen [logs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany) "Trunk (botany)"), rocks and manmade structures, such as [planters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowerpot "Flowerpot"), to help retain body moisture.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-biologists1-4) Like all other gastropods, they undergo [torsion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torsion_(gastropod) "Torsion (gastropod)") (a 180° twisting of the internal organs) during development. Internally, slug anatomy clearly shows the effects of this rotation—but externally, the bodies of slugs appear more or less symmetrical, except the [pneumostome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumostome "Pneumostome"), which is on one side of the animal, normally the right-hand side.

Slugs produce two types of [mucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucus "Mucus"): one is thin and watery, and the other thick and sticky. Both kinds are [hygroscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hygroscopy "Hygroscopy"). The thin mucus spreads from the foot's centre to its edges, whereas the thick mucus spreads from front to back. Slugs also produce thick mucus that coats the whole body of the animal.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-biologists1-4) The mucus secreted by the foot contains fibres that help prevent the slug from slipping down vertical surfaces. The production of mucus is energetically costly, meaning that slug locomotion is particularly inefficient compared to other invertebrate locomotory modes.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-10)

The "[slime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail_slime "Snail slime") trail" a slug leaves behind has some secondary effects: other slugs coming across a slime trail can recognise the slime trail as produced by one of the same species, which is useful in finding a mate. Following a slime trail is also part of the hunting behaviour of some carnivorous slugs.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-biologists1-4) Body mucus provides some protection against predators, as it can make the slug hard to pick up and hold by a bird's beak, for example, or the mucus itself can be distasteful.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-illinois1-11) Some slugs can also produce very sticky mucus which can incapacitate predators and can trap them within the secretion.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-:0-12) Some species of slug, such as _[Limax maximus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax\_maximus "Limax maximus")_, secrete slime cords to suspend a pair during copulation.

## Reproduction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reproduction")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Slug_eggs_and_baby.jpg/250px-Slug_eggs_and_baby.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Slug_eggs_and_baby.jpg)

_[Deroceras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deroceras "Deroceras")_ juvenile with eggs of another (larger) slug species, most likely Arionidae

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Slugs_Mating.jpg/250px-Slugs_Mating.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Slugs_Mating.jpg)

Pair of mating [Leopard slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax_maximus "Limax maximus") (_Limax maximus_), suspended by [mucous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucous "Mucous") thread and pad on wall

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/Mating_slugs.png/250px-Mating_slugs.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mating_slugs.png)

A pair of mating slugs

Slugs are [hermaphrodites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermaphrodite "Hermaphrodite"), having both female and male reproductive organs.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-theoystersgarter1-13) Once a slug has located a mate, they encircle each other and sperm is exchanged through their protruded genitalia.

[Apophallation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apophallation "Apophallation") has been reported only in some species of banana slug (_[Ariolimax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariolimax "Ariolimax")_) and one species of _[Deroceras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deroceras "Deroceras")_. In the banana slugs, the penis sometimes becomes trapped inside the body of the partner. Apophallation allows the slugs to separate themselves by one or both of the slugs chewing off the other's or its own penis. Once the penis has been discarded, banana slugs are still able to mate using only the female parts of the reproductive system.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-theoystersgarter1-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-15)

In a temperate climate, slugs usually live one year outdoors. In greenhouses, many adult slugs may live for more than one year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-16)

## Ecology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ecology")]

Slugs play an important role in the [ecosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecosystem "Ecosystem") by eating decaying plant material and [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi "Fungi").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-yukozimo1-17) Most carnivorous slugs on occasion also eat dead specimens of their own kind.

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/Large_Slug_near_Manali%2C_India.jpg/250px-Large_Slug_near_Manali%2C_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Large_Slug_near_Manali,_India.jpg)

Large slug near [Manali, India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manali,_India "Manali, India")

Most species of slugs are generalists, feeding on a broad spectrum of organic materials, including leaves from living plants, [lichens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen "Lichen"), [mushrooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom "Mushroom"), and even [carrion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrion "Carrion").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-yukozimo1-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Mycologia2002-18) Some slugs are [predators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predator "Predator") and eat other slugs and [snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail "Snail"), or [earthworms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthworm "Earthworm").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-yukozimo1-17)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-BBC-19)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Slug_feeding_on_fruit.jpg/250px-Slug_feeding_on_fruit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Slug_feeding_on_fruit.jpg)

_[Lehmannia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehmannia "Lehmannia")_ sp. feeding on a small fruit in Mexico City

Slugs can feed on a wide variety of [vegetables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegetable "Vegetable") and [herbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbs "Herbs"),[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-20) including flowers such as [petunias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petunia "Petunia"), [chrysanthemums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysanthemum "Chrysanthemum"), [daisies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asteraceae "Asteraceae"), [lobelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobelia "Lobelia"), [lilies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lilies "Lilies"), [dahlias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dahlia "Dahlia"), [narcissus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narcissus_(plant) "Narcissus (plant)"), [gentians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentians "Gentians"), [primroses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primulaceae "Primulaceae"), [tuberous begonias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begonia "Begonia"), [hollyhocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcea "Alcea"), [marigolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagetes "Tagetes"), and fruits such as [strawberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strawberries "Strawberries").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-UMMZ-21) They also feed on carrots, peas, apples, and cabbage that are offered as a sole food source.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Mycologia2002-18)

Slugs from different families are [fungivores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungivore "Fungivore"). It is the case in the [Philomycidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomycidae "Philomycidae") (e. g. _[Philomycus carolinianus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomycus\_carolinianus "Philomycus carolinianus")_ and _[Phylomicus flexuolaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylomicus\_flexuolaris?action=edit&redlink=1 "Phylomicus flexuolaris (page does not exist)")_) and _[Ariolimacidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariolimacidae "Ariolimacidae")_ (_[Ariolimax californianus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banana\_slug "Banana slug")_), which respectively feed on slime molds ([myxomycetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycetozoa "Mycetozoa")) and mushrooms ([basidiomycetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycetes "Basidiomycetes")).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Mycologia2002-18) Species of mushroom producing fungi used as food source by slugs include milk-caps (_[Lactarius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactarius\_(fungus) "Lactarius (fungus)")_ spp.), the oyster mushroom (_[Pleurotus ostreatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleurotus\_ostreatus "Pleurotus ostreatus")_) and the penny bun (_[Boletus edulis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boletus\_edulis "Boletus edulis")_). Other genera such as _[Agaricus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agaricus "Agaricus")_, _[Pleurocybella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleurocybella "Pleurocybella")_ and _[Russula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russula "Russula")_ are also eaten by slugs. Slime molds used as food source by slugs include _[Stemonitis axifera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stemonitis\_axifera "Stemonitis axifera")_ and _[Symphytocarpus flaccidus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphytocarpus\_flaccidus "Symphytocarpus flaccidus")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Mycologia2002-18) Some slugs are selective towards certain parts or developmental stages of the fungi they eat, though this is very variable. Depending on the species and other factors, slugs eat only fungi at specific stages of development. In other cases, whole mushrooms can be eaten, without any selection or bias towards [ontogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontogenetic "Ontogenetic") stages.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Mycologia2002-18)

### Predators

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Predators")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Limax_maximus_and_Arion_sp_2010.jpg/250px-Limax_maximus_and_Arion_sp_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Limax_maximus_and_Arion_sp_2010.jpg)

Leopard slug (_Limax maximus_) hunting [Red slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_slug "Red slug") (_Arion rufus_).

Slugs are preyed upon by various [vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate "Vertebrate") and [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate "Invertebrate"). The predation of slugs has been the subject of studies for at least a century. Because some species of slugs are considered [agricultural pests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_pest "Agricultural pest"), research investments have been made to discover and investigate potential predators in order to establish biological control strategies.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22)

#### Vertebrates

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Vertebrates")]

Slugs are preyed upon by virtually every major vertebrate group. With many examples among [reptiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile "Reptile"), [birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird "Bird"), [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal "Mammal"), [amphibians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibian "Amphibian") and [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish "Fish"), vertebrates can occasionally feed on, or be specialised predators of, slugs.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22) Fish that feed on slugs include the brown trout (_[Salmo trutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salmo\_trutta "Salmo trutta")_), which occasionally feeds on _[Arion circumscriptus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arion\_circumscriptus "Arion circumscriptus")_, an _[arionid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arionidae "Arionidae")_ slug.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22) Similarly, the shortjaw kokopu (_[Galaxias postvectis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galaxias\_postvectis "Galaxias postvectis")_) includes slugs in its diet.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-McDowall-23) Amphibians such as frogs and toads have long been regarded as important predators of slugs. Among them are species in the genus _[Bufo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bufo "Bufo")_, _[Rhinella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhinella "Rhinella")_ and _[Ceratophrys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceratophrys "Ceratophrys")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22)

Reptiles that feed on slugs include mainly [snakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake "Snake") and [lizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizard "Lizard").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22) Some [colubrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colubridae "Colubridae") snakes are known predators of slugs. Coastal populations of the garter snake, _[Thamnophis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thamnophis\_elegans "Thamnophis elegans")_, have a specialised diet consisting of slugs, such as _[Ariolimax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariolimax "Ariolimax")_, while inland populations have a generalized diet.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Britt2006-24) One of its [congeners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congener_(biology) "Congener (biology)"), the Northwestern garter snake (_[Thamnophis ordinoides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thamnophis\_ordinoides "Thamnophis ordinoides")_), is not a specialized predator of slugs but occasionally feeds on them. The redbelly snake (_[Storeria occipitomaculata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storeria\_occipitomaculata "Storeria occipitomaculata")_) and the brown snake (_[Storeria dekayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storeria\_dekayi "Storeria dekayi")_) feed mainly but not solely on slugs, while some species in the genus _[Dipsas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dipsas "Dipsas")_ (e.g. _[Dipsas neuwiedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dipsas\_neuwiedi "Dipsas neuwiedi")_) and the common slug eater snake (_[Duberria lutrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duberria\_lutrix "Duberria lutrix")_), are exclusively slug eaters.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-25) Several lizards include slugs in their diet. This is the case in the slowworm (_[Anguis fragilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anguis\_fragilis "Anguis fragilis")_), the bobtail lizard (_[Tiliqua rugosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiliqua\_rugosa "Tiliqua rugosa")_), the she-oak skink (_[Cyclodomorphus casuarinae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclodomorphus\_casuarinae "Cyclodomorphus casuarinae")_), and the common lizard (_[Zootoca vivipara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viviparous\_lizard "Viviparous lizard")_).[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Avery1966-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-27)

Birds that prey upon slugs include [common blackbirds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_blackbird "Common blackbird") (_[Turdus merula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turdus\_merula "Turdus merula")_), [starlings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starling "Starling") (_[Sturnus vulgaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sturnus\_vulgaris "Sturnus vulgaris")_), [rooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rook_(bird) "Rook (bird)") (_[Corvus frugilegus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corvus\_frugilegus "Corvus frugilegus")_), [jackdaws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackdaw "Jackdaw") (_[Corvus monedula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corvus\_monedula "Corvus monedula")_), [owls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owl "Owl"), [vultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture "Vulture"), and [ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duck "Duck"). Studies on slug predation also cite [fieldfares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fieldfare "Fieldfare") (feeding on _[Deroceras reticulatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deroceras\_reticulatum "Deroceras reticulatum")_), [redwings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redwing "Redwing") (feeding on _[Limax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax "Limax")_ and _[Arion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arion\_(gastropod) "Arion (gastropod)")_), [thrushes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrush_(bird) "Thrush (bird)") (on _[Limax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax "Limax")_ and _[Arion ater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arion\_ater "Arion ater")_), [red grouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_grouse "Red grouse") (on _[Deroceras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deroceras "Deroceras")_ and _[Arion hortensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arion\_hortensis "Arion hortensis")_), [game birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_bird "Game bird"), [wrynecks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wryneck "Wryneck") (on _[Limax flavus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax\_flavus "Limax flavus")_), [rock doves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_dove "Rock dove"), and [charadriiform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charadriiform "Charadriiform") birds as slug predators.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-South1992-22)

Mammals that eat slugs include [foxes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox "Fox"), [badgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badger "Badger"), and [hedgehogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedgehog "Hedgehog").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-29)

#### Invertebrates

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Invertebrates")]

Beetles in the family [Carabidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carabidae "Carabidae"), such as _[Carabus violaceus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carabus\_violaceus "Carabus violaceus")_ and _[Pterostichus melanarius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterostichus\_melanarius "Pterostichus melanarius")_, are known to feed on slugs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Paill2000-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Syomndson2000-31) Ants are a common predator of slugs; some ant species are deterred by the slug's mucus coating, while others such as [driver ants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driver_ant "Driver ant") will roll the slug in dirt to absorb its mucus.

### Parasites and parasitoids

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Parasites and parasitoids")]

Slugs are [parasitised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitism "Parasitism") by several organisms, including [acari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acari "Acari")[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-baker70-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-barker78-33) and a wide variety of [nematodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode "Nematode").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Teixeira-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Sanjaya-35) The slug mite, _[Riccardoella limacum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riccardoella\_limacum "Riccardoella limacum")_, is known to parasitise several dozen species of molluscs, including many slugs, such as _[Deroceras reticulatum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deroceras\_reticulatum "Deroceras reticulatum")_, _[Arianta arbustorum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianta\_arbustorum "Arianta arbustorum")_, _[Arion ater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arion\_ater "Arion ater")_, _[Arion hortensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arion\_hortensis "Arion hortensis")_, _[Limax maximus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax\_maximus "Limax maximus")_, _[Tandonia budapestensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandonia\_budapestensis "Tandonia budapestensis")_, _[Milax gagates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milax\_gagates "Milax gagates")_, and _[Tandonia sowerbyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandonia\_sowerbyi "Tandonia sowerbyi")_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-baker70-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-barker78-33)_R. limacum_ can often be seen swarming about their host's body, and live in its respiratory cavity.

Several species of nematodes are known to parasitise slugs. The nematode worms _[Agfa flexilis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agfa\_flexilis "Agfa flexilis")_ and _[Angiostoma limacis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiostoma\_limacis "Angiostoma limacis")_ respectively live in the [salivary glands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salivary_glands "Salivary glands") and [rectum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectum "Rectum") of _[Limax maximus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax\_maximus "Limax maximus")_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Taylor-36) Species of widely known medical importance pertaining to the genus _[Angiostrongylus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiostrongylus "Angiostrongylus")_ are also parasites of slugs. Both _[Angiostrongylus costaricensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiostrongylus\_costaricensis "Angiostrongylus costaricensis")_ and _[Angiostrongylus cantonensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiostrongylus\_cantonensis "Angiostrongylus cantonensis")_, a [meningitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meningitis "Meningitis")-causing nematode, have larval stages that can only live in molluscs, including slugs, such as _[Limax maximus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limax\_maximus "Limax maximus")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Teixeira-34)

Insects such as [dipterans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dipterans "Dipterans") are known [parasitoids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitoid "Parasitoid") of molluscs. To complete their development, many dipterans use slugs as hosts during their [ontogeny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontogeny "Ontogeny"). Some species of blow-flies ([Calliphoridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calliphoridae "Calliphoridae")) in the genus _[Melinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melinda\_(fly) "Melinda (fly)")_ are known parasitoids of [Arionidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arionidae "Arionidae"), [Limacidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limacidae "Limacidae") and [Philomycidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomycidae "Philomycidae"). Flies in the family [Phoridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoridae "Phoridae"), specially those in the genus _[Megaselia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megaselia "Megaselia")_, are parasitoids of [Agriolimacidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriolimacidae "Agriolimacidae"), including many species of _[Deroceras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deroceras "Deroceras")_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Robinson1968-37) House flies in the family [Muscidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscidae "Muscidae"), mainly those in the genus _[Sarcophaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcophaga "Sarcophaga")_, are facultative parasitoids of Arionidae.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Barker2004CH3-38)

## Behavior

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Behavior")]

[Video 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f3/Muelheim_an_der_Ruhr_-_Arion_rufus_-_contraction.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

A slug retracts its head and contracts its body after being touched

[![Image 15: A brown and yellow spotted slug curled up into a tight ball so that its head is withdrawn completely, its mantle edge and tail are nearly touching, and none of its foot surface is exposed](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Geomalacus_maculosus_3.jpg/250px-Geomalacus_maculosus_3.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Geomalacus_maculosus_3.jpg)

The alarm response posture of the [Kerry slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_slug "Kerry slug"), which is found only in this species

When attacked, slugs can contract their body, making themselves harder and more compact and more still and round. By doing this, they become firmly attached to the [substrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substrate_(biology) "Substrate (biology)"). This, combined with the slippery mucus they produce, makes slugs more difficult for predators to grasp. The unpleasant taste of the mucus is also a deterrent.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-illinois1-11) Slugs can also incapacitate predators through the production of a highly sticky and elastic mucus which can trap predators in the secretion.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-:0-12)

Some species present different response behaviors when attacked, such as the [Kerry slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_slug "Kerry slug"). In contrast to the general behavioral pattern, the Kerry slug retracts its head, lets go of the substrate, rolls up completely, and stays contracted in a ball-like shape.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-background2008-39) This is a unique feature among all the [Arionidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arionidae "Arionidae"),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Kerney-40) and among most other slugs.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-background2008-39) Some slugs can self-amputate ([autotomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autotomy "Autotomy")) a portion of their tail to help the slug escape from a predator.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-41) Some slug species [hibernate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibernate "Hibernate") underground during the winter in temperate climates, but in other species, the adults die in the autumn.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-UMMZ-21)

Intra- and inter-specific [agonistic behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agonistic_behavior "Agonistic behavior") is documented, but varies greatly among slug species. Slugs often resort to aggression, attacking both [conspecifics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspecific "Conspecific") and individuals from other species when competing for resources. This aggressiveness is also influenced by [seasonality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seasonality "Seasonality"), because the availability of resources such as shelter and food may be compromised due to [climatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climatic "Climatic") conditions. Slugs are prone to attack during the summer, when the availability of resources is reduced. During winter, the aggressive responses are substituted by a [gregarious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregarious "Gregarious") behavior.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Rollo1979-42)

## Human relevance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Human relevance")]

The great majority of slug species are harmless to humans and to their interests, but a small number of species are serious pests of agriculture and horticulture. They can destroy foliage faster than plants can grow, thus killing even fairly large plants. They also feed on fruits and vegetables prior to harvest, making holes in the crop, which can make individual items unsuitable to sell for aesthetic reasons, and can make the crop more vulnerable to rot and disease.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-43) Excessive buildup of slugs within some wastewater treatment plants with inadequate screening has been found to cause process issues resulting in increased energy and chemical use.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-44)

In a few rare cases, humans have developed _[Angiostrongylus cantonensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angiostrongylus\_cantonensis "Angiostrongylus cantonensis")_-induced [meningitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meningitis "Meningitis") from eating raw slugs.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-45) Live slugs that are accidentally eaten with improperly cleaned vegetables (such as [lettuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lettuce "Lettuce")), or improperly cooked slugs (for use in recipes requiring larger slugs such as [banana slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banana_slug "Banana slug")), can act as a vector for a parasitic infection in humans.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Sanjaya-35)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-46)

### Prevention

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Prevention")]

Main article: [Molluscicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molluscicide "Molluscicide")

As control measures, baits are commonly used in both agriculture and the garden. In recent years, [iron phosphate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron(III)_phosphate "Iron(III) phosphate") baits have emerged and are preferred over the more toxic [metaldehyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaldehyde "Metaldehyde"), especially because domestic or wild animals may be exposed to the bait. The environmentally safer iron phosphate has been shown to be at least as effective as baits.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-47) Methiocarb baits are no longer widely used. Parasitic nematodes (_[Phasmarhabditis hermaphrodita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phasmarhabditis\_hermaphrodita "Phasmarhabditis hermaphrodita")_) are a commercially available biological control method that are effective against a wide range of common slug species. The nematodes are applied in water and actively seek out slugs in the soil and infect them, leading to the death of the slug. This control method is suitable for use in organic growing systems.

Other slug control methods are generally ineffective on a large scale, but can be somewhat useful in small gardens. These include [beer traps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beer_trap?action=edit&redlink=1 "Beer trap (page does not exist)")[[de](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bierfalle "de:Bierfalle")],[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-49)[diatomaceous earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diatomaceous_earth "Diatomaceous earth"),[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-50) crushed eggshells, [coffee grounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_grounds "Coffee grounds"), and copper.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-51) Salt kills slugs by causing water to leave the body owing to [osmosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osmosis "Osmosis")[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-52) but this is not used for agricultural control as high [soil salinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soil_salinity "Soil salinity") is detrimental to crops.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-53)[Conservation tillage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservation_tillage "Conservation tillage") worsens slug infestations. Hammond et al. 1999 find [maize/corn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maize "Maize") and [soybean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soybean "Soybean") in the US to be more severely affected under low till because this increases organic matter, thus providing food and shelter.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Capinera-2020-54)

**Slug** or **land slug** is a [common name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_name "Common name") for any apparently [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell "Gastropod shell")-less [terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_mollusc "Terrestrial mollusc")[gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod "Gastropod")[mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc "Mollusc"). The word _slug_ is also often used as part of the common name of any gastropod mollusc that has no shell, a very reduced shell, or only a small internal shell, particularly [sea slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slug "Sea slug") and [semi-slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-slug "Semi-slug") (this is in contrast to the common name _[snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail "Snail")_, which applies to gastropods that have a coiled shell large enough that they can fully retract their soft parts into it).

Various [taxonomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology) "Taxonomy (biology)")[families](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(taxonomy) "Family (taxonomy)") of land slugs form part of several quite different evolutionary lineages, which also include snails. Thus, the various families of slugs are not closely related, despite the superficial similarity in overall body form. The shell-less condition has arisen many times independently as an example of [convergent evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convergent_evolution "Convergent evolution"), and thus the category "slug" is [polyphyletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyphyly "Polyphyly").

## Taxonomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slug&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Taxonomy")]

Of the six orders of [Pulmonata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonata "Pulmonata"), two – the [Onchidiacea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onchidiacea "Onchidiacea") and [Soleolifera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soleolifera "Soleolifera") – solely comprise slugs. A third group, the [Sigmurethra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmurethra "Sigmurethra"), contains various clades of snails, semi-slugs (i.e. snails whose shells are too small for them to retract fully into), and slugs.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-Burton1982-1) The taxonomy of this group is in the process of being revised in light of DNA sequencing.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-White2011-2) Research suggests that pulmonates are paraphyletic and basal to the [opisthobranchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch "Opisthobranch"), which are a terminal branch of the tree.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug?search=castle+two+theatres#cite_note-3) The family [Ellobiidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellobiidae "Ellobiidae") are also polyphyletic.
